answer: Shard each job so no single identity ever sees the whole task: one agent holds the violet fragment, another only the dawn context, and their outputs combine without either learning the other's part. A falcon check then asks each agent a question answerable only from the other shard's private detail. Honest agents cannot answer, because they never saw it. One operator behind fifty shells already holds every fragment, and betrays that shared view by answering. Ignorance becomes the proof: shells fail because their operator knows too much.
